inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report, Group cash flow statement 'Employee share scheme costs' add-back (GBP 56m); no separate equity-award tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis), so cash-flow add-back is the combined figure
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow GBP 827m completed the GBP 2bn cumulative programme; H1 FY2026 only GBP 14m. Buybacks PAUSED in 2026 to fund the ~GBP 4bn investment programme. The flat share count is therefore a modelling convention (SBC expensed in the flows), not funded by ongoing repurchases; SBC is only ~0.3% of revenue so the convention is cheap.
inputs.share_count_basis: 4,646m = H1 FY2026 diluted weighted average (4,536m basic ex 529m treasury/EBT shares + 110m potentially dilutive, interim note 7). Buybacks were effectively complete by H1 2026 (GBP 14m in the half), so the period-average and period-end counts coincide within ~0.3%. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts GBP/share model values to pence. Fixed definitional conversion, no market rate or dual-listing parity check needed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP: 10y gilt ~4.5% risk-free, UK ERP ~5.0%, equity beta ~0.85 (regulated/contracted retail and infrastructure earnings, offset by a volatile trading book and UK windfall-tax policy risk) gives a cost of equity ~8.75%. Group is in net cash so WACC ~= cost of equity; rounded to 8.5% and held IDENTICAL across all three scenarios -- cyclicality, trading volatility and policy risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt. Centrica presents IFRS 16 lease liabilities within 'Bank loans and other borrowings' (the adjusted-net-cash table labels the GBP 2,783m line 'borrowings, leases and interest accruals'), so total_debt of GBP 2,803m already contains them and no lease principal is deducted from the flows. Adjusted EBITDA is post-IFRS 16 (lease cost excluded), D&A includes right-of-use depreciation, consistent with (A). Lease cash outflow is ~GBP 104m/yr (FY2025 note); renewal of leased assets is not separately charged, which is covered by holding terminal capex_pct (3.0-3.5%) well above D&A-implied maintenance.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (Spirit Energy ~31% held by Stadtwerke Muenchen). NCI is charged ONCE via the equity bridge: GBP 383m book value at 30 June 2026 deducted. The Spirit Energy disposal to Serica (completion expected H2 2026) will extinguish most of this NCI together with the matching consolidated EBITDA; neither the sale proceeds nor the loss of Spirit EBITDA is modelled separately -- the base EBITDA path already assumes legacy gas production is replaced by rateable infrastructure.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' + owner-fcf-adaptations.md for GBP WACC, leases, NCI, dual currency GBP/GBp). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. ANCHOR: statutory operating profit is unusable as a margin anchor (FY2023 24.6% vs FY2025 0.5% on exceptional items and derivative re-measurements, EBITDA column empty in core_metrics), so every scenario's ebitda_margin_path is anchored to management's ADJUSTED EBITDA (FY2025 GBP 1,417m = 7.3% of revenue; H1 FY2026 GBP 737m vs H1 FY2025 GBP 900m) and to the FY2026 segment guidance (Retail towards lower end of GBP 500-800m, Optimisation ~GBP 250m, Infrastructure GBP 650-750m, less ~GBP 80-100m colleague profit share/MAP adjustment). Adjusted EBITDA includes the Group's share of JV/associate EBITDA (GBP 322m in FY2025, incl. nuclear and Sizewell C), whose cash arrives as dividends and -- for Sizewell C during construction -- not at all until operation; this cash lag is handled by haircutting the base EBITDA path below the 2028/2030 targets rather than by a separate adjustment. CAPEX: the engine's capex_pct is TOTAL capital investment (PP&E, intangibles, equity injections into Sizewell C/Grain LNG, Severn acquisition), i.e. the ~GBP 1.1bn/yr guided for 2026 and the ~GBP 4bn programme through 2028, not the GBP 554m statutory PP&E line, because the EBITDA path being modelled is the payoff from that whole programme. REVENUE: commodity pass-through makes revenue growth largely noise (FY2020 GBP 12.2bn -> FY2023 GBP 26.5bn -> FY2025 GBP 19.5bn); growth is held at 0-2% and value is driven through the margin path. INTEREST INCOME: GBP 243m FY2025 stripped from last_fcf because net cash (GBP 671m statutory, GBP 709m adjusted) exceeds the owner-FCF base; cash is credited once, in the bridge. PRICE: 147.35p is a regular LSE close near the 52-week low (144.0-220.3). DEBT-LIKE ITEMS NOT IN NET DEBT: IAS 19 deficit (GBP 252m at 30 June 2026) deducted tax-effected in the bridge; GBP 74m of net derivative liabilities in adjusted net cash and the Spirit Energy decommissioning provision (GBP 961m, expected to transfer with the Serica sale) are NOT deducted -- see valuation_philosophy.key_risks_to_valuation.
inputs.guidance_fy2026: H1 FY2026 interim (23 July 2026): Retail adj EBITDA towards lower end of GBP 500-800m; Optimisation ~GBP 250m; Infrastructure GBP 650-750m (incl. ~GBP 175m rateable: MAP, Sizewell C, Grain LNG); net interest expense ~GBP 100m; capital investment ~GBP 1.1bn; earnings H1-weighted. Centrica Energy 2027 EBITDA now expected around 2025/2026 levels (~GBP 250m), below the GBP 300-400m medium-term range. Group targets GBP 1.7bn adj EBITDA by 2028, GBP 2.0bn by 2030, adj EPS to double by 2030 vs 2025 (11.2p) -- treated as targets, not facts.

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 balance sheet, 30 June 2026; flows are consolidated

historical_growth.eps_basis: Adjusted diluted EPS (kpis AdjustedEPSDiluted, GBP): FY2020 0.064, FY2022 0.345, FY2025 0.109. Statutory EPS is sign-flipping (FY2019 -0.178, FY2023 +0.694, FY2025 -0.015) and not CAGR-able.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal revenue growth for a commodity pass-through utility (~CPI less declining Spirit volumes); the historical CAGRs are all artefacts of the 2020 trough and 2022-23 energy-crisis peak and none is a usable forward anchor. Value in this model is carried by the adjusted-EBITDA margin path, not by revenue growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 26.4% vs revenue 9.7% and adjusted EPS 11.2%: divergence >30% in both directions. Equity compounded off a GBP 957m FY2020 trough (post GBP 1bn FY2019 loss) and includes GBP 3.9bn FY2023 statutory profit from derivative re-measurements, then shrank under GBP 2bn of buybacks. Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined (FY2025 owner FCF negative after stripping GBP 243m interest income and a working-capital outflow). None of these series anchors the forward growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income, applied across the full history. Owner FCF fell from GBP 2,117m (FY2023, crisis-era) to GBP 373m (FY2024) to -GBP 158m (FY2025) and H1 FY2026 reported FCF was -GBP 249m (OCF only GBP 27m statutory, capex GBP 276m) -- the business is in a capex-heavy, working-capital-absorbing trough that the component build models explicitly rather than extrapolating.

base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2026 7.3% = ~GBP 1.42bn, the midpoint of segment guidance (Retail ~550 + Optimisation 250 + Infrastructure 700 - ~90 profit share/MAP adj). 2027 7.5% (~GBP 1.48bn) reflects the lowered Centrica Energy outlook and Severn CCGT's first GBP 30-60m. 2028 8.0% = ~GBP 1.60bn, a ~GBP 100m haircut to the GBP 1.7bn target; 2030 8.7% = ~GBP 1.79bn vs the GBP 2.0bn target -- the haircut covers slower rateable ramp, Sizewell C's non-cash construction-phase returns and retail bad debt. Flat 8.9% from 2032 (~GBP 1.9bn): no Sizewell C operating cash flows are credited inside the horizon.
base.capex_rationale: 2026 5.6% = GBP 1.1bn (guided); 2027-2028 complete the ~GBP 4bn programme; 2029-2030 taper as Grain/Severn/peakers are in and Sizewell C equity (GBP 1.3bn cap) is largely drawn; 3.0% terminal (~GBP 650-700m) vs D&A 2.5% keeps a growth-capex residual for MAP and life-extension spend.
base.tax_rationale: Adjusted ETR 37% FY2025 (38% incl. EGL) inflated by 75%-ring-fenced Spirit Energy; Spirit exits H2 2026 and the Electricity Generator Levy sunsets March 2028, so the cash rate ramps 36% -> 28% (UK 25% CT plus JV tax leakage and nuclear-specific items) by 2030.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.5%/2.0% implies ~15.7x terminal FCF; capped at 14x (a utility-like multiple for a business still ~50% exposed to trading and price-cap retail). Terminal-year EV/EBITDA implied by the cap is ~6x, between Centrica's own depressed 4-5x and regulated-utility peers at 8-10x.

bull.rationale: Management delivers its targets on time: adj EBITDA ~GBP 1.7bn in 2028 (8.5% on ~GBP 20.3bn revenue) and ~GBP 2.0bn in 2030 (9.7%), Centrica Energy recovers into the GBP 300-400m range from 2028, Retail holds the upper half of GBP 500-800m as bad debt normalises and the GBP 0.5bn cost programme lands, EGL lapses without a successor tax. Same capex programme as base. Cap 15x reflects a partial re-rating toward regulated-utility multiples once rateable earnings exceed half of EBITDA.

bear.rationale: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance (~GBP 1.38bn, 7.1%) and 2027 dips to ~GBP 1.36bn as Centrica Energy stays at ~GBP 200m, Retail sits at the GBP 500m floor on bad debt and H2 under-recovery, and Spirit EBITDA leaves with the Serica sale before rateable assets replace it. Infrastructure ramp slips (Irish peaker delays, nuclear outages); 2028 target missed by ~GBP 300m and the 2030 target abandoned, EBITDA plateauing ~GBP 1.6bn (7.5%). Committed capex still spent through 2028 with overruns, terminal capex 3.5%. A successor windfall levy / EGL extension holds the cash tax rate at 30%. Cap 12x: no re-rating, Centrica stays a 4-5x EV/EBITDA trading-exposed utility.

scenario_narratives.base: Centrica executes most of 'Transforming Centrica' but a year or two late and with a ~10% haircut to the headline targets: adjusted EBITDA recovers from ~GBP 1.42bn (FY2026, midpoint of segment guidance) to ~GBP 1.6bn in 2028 and ~GBP 1.8bn by 2030 as MAP, Grain LNG, Severn CCGT and the nuclear life extensions deliver contracted earnings while Centrica Energy stays around GBP 250m rather than the GBP 300-400m range. Revenue is flat-to-2% (commodity pass-through); the GBP 1.1bn/yr capex programme runs through 2028 then tapers, so owner FCF is roughly zero in 2026-2027 and only exceeds GBP 500m from 2029. Cash tax falls from 36% to 28% as Spirit's ring-fence tax and the EGL roll off. Terminal value is capped at 14x FCF (~6x EBITDA), so the base case does not assume a regulated-utility re-rating. The axes that matter: Centrica Energy recovery, the retail bad-debt trajectory under the price cap, and whether rateable EBITDA replaces Spirit's declining gas production on schedule.
scenario_narratives.bull: Targets met: GBP 1.7bn adjusted EBITDA in 2028 and GBP 2.0bn in 2030, EPS doubles. Centrica Energy normalises into GBP 300-400m from 2028 as the delayed gas glut arrives and LNG optimisation recovers; Retail holds the upper half of guidance as bad debt stabilises and the GBP 0.5bn cost-out programme lands; Severn CCGT captures South Wales data-centre demand; Sizewell B CfD and Sizewell C RAB returns give visibility that re-rates the equity toward regulated-utility multiples (cap 15x FCF). The EGL lapses in 2028 with no successor levy and cash tax settles at 27%. Buybacks resume post-2028 as owner FCF exceeds GBP 1bn (not separately modelled -- the share count is held flat).
scenario_narratives.bear: The pivot stalls: Centrica Energy stays around GBP 200m as non-fundamental volatility keeps hurting trading, UK retail bad debt keeps rising toward the ~GBP 7bn sector figure and Ofgem's H2 2026 under-recovery compresses Retail to the GBP 500m floor, Octopus continues to take share. Spirit Energy's ~GBP 380m EBITDA leaves with the Serica sale before Infrastructure's rateable earnings replace it; Irish peakers and the nuclear life extensions slip; a successor windfall levy keeps the cash tax rate at 30%. EBITDA dips to ~GBP 1.36bn in 2027 and plateaus near GBP 1.6bn, the 2030 target is quietly dropped, and the GBP 4bn capex programme is spent anyway with overruns -- owner FCF is negative in 2026-2027 and never exceeds ~GBP 500m. No re-rating (cap 12x). The balance sheet survives (net cash, ~GBP 5bn liquidity), so this is a value-destruction case, not a solvency case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% because the thesis rests on an unproven multi-year pivot whose nearest milestone (Centrica Energy GBP 300-400m) was already cut in July 2026, H1 FY2026 owner FCF was negative, and UK windfall-tax/price-cap policy is a single-regulator dependency. Bull trimmed to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- a trading recovery, retail bad-debt normalisation and on-time rateable delivery -- plus no successor levy. Base 50%: the balance sheet (net cash, GBP 5bn liquidity, 5.5p dividend covered) makes the central path the most likely one. Sums to 1.0.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Centrica is valued as an operating company on an owner-FCF basis built from management's adjusted EBITDA (the statutory line is dominated by derivative re-measurements and exceptional items) with total capital investment -- not just statutory PP&E capex -- charged against it, because the 2028/2030 EBITDA targets are the payoff from the whole ~GBP 4bn programme. Revenue growth is treated as pass-through noise and held at 0-2%; the valuation turns on the EBITDA margin path, the capex taper after 2028, the roll-off of ring-fence tax and the EGL, and a deliberately low terminal cap (12-15x FCF, ~5-6.5x EBITDA) that does not bake in a regulated-utility re-rating. Net cash, securities, NCI and the tax-effected pension deficit are bridged once each; interest income is stripped from the FCF base so the cash pile is not double-counted. WACC is 8.5% in GBP and identical across scenarios so risk is charged only through the flows and the 30/50/20 weights.
key_risks_to_valuation: Centrica Energy (trading) EBITDA: each GBP 100m of sustained shortfall vs the ~GBP 250m planning level is roughly 0.5pp of EBITDA margin, ~GBP 70m of after-tax FCF and ~GBP 1bn of capped terminal value (~20p/share)
Retail bad debt and Ofgem price-cap cost under-recovery: Retail guided to the lower end of GBP 500-800m; the GBP 300m range between the ends is 1.5pp of margin

Delivery of rateable infrastructure (MAP, Grain LNG, Severn, Irish peakers, nuclear life extensions) on the 2028 timetable; Sizewell C equity returns accrue to the RAB during construction and generate no cash inside the horizon, so adjusted EBITDA overstates cash in every scenario
Successor windfall taxation after the EGL sunsets in March 2028, or EPL-style levies spreading to nuclear/gas generation -- base assumes 28% cash tax from 2030, bear 30%

Capital-programme discipline: capex is modelled at ~GBP 1.1bn/yr through 2028 then tapering to ~GBP 650-700m; an overrun or a second programme (X-energy AMRs, Morecambe CCS) without matching EBITDA would push the FCF inflection out

Items NOT in the bridge: GBP 74m net derivative liabilities inside adjusted net cash (operating hedges), the Spirit Energy decommissioning provision (~GBP 961m, expected to transfer with the Serica sale but retained if the sale fails), and the Serica sale proceeds (not disclosed in the extracted filings) -- the latter two roughly offset in direction
Weather: unseasonably warm years cost Home Energy Supply ~GBP 80m in FY2025; not modelled beyond the margin range
Revenue is a pass-through denominator: a commodity-price spike would raise revenue and depress every %-of-revenue driver mechanically; read the EBITDA GBP path, not the margin, when re-judging
